candidate_windows.window_text:
In all experiments, for the generating stage in Sec. 2.2, we use a pre-trained $\mathrm{BERT}_{\mathrm{LARGE}}$ model (Devlin et al., 2019) for the beam search. In particular, we use the mean operation over the multi-head attention weights from the last layer of $\mathrm{BERT}_{\mathrm{LARGE}}$ according to the parameter study in (Wang et al., 2020). For the ranking model in Sec. 2.2, we use the pre-trained $\mathrm{BERT}_{\mathrm{BASE}}$ model. We use the implementations of the pretrained language models (LM) in the Transformers package (Wolf et al., 2020).

To keep our framework simple, we use the same hyperparameters across the majority of our experiments. For generating, we use: 8 GeForce RTX 2080 Ti GPUs with a batch size of 16 per GPU; maximum sequence length as 256 tokens. For datasets that provide examples beyond sentence level, we adopt spaCy sentencizer to segment the texts into sentences, and each sample in the batch is a sentence. For ranking, we experiment with: 1 NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU with a batch size of 8 per GPU; the AdamW optimizer (Kingma and Ba, 2015); linear learning rate decay starting from $10^{-6}$ ; maximum sequence length as 512 tokens. The top-1 triple from ranking model is returned except for OIE2016 (open information extraction) since it provides a dev set. We additionally report results of top-10 triples for relation classification (FewRel and TACRED).

In the rest of this section, we describe datasets, comparison methods, additional implementation details for each information extraction task, as well as more experimental insights. Results of all experiments are in Table 1. We use the default evaluation metrics for each task as below. We show more input and output formats on all datasets in Table 7.
